passage:
First week of June. Sarika, who had guided Lavanya through her first two years at the Jaipur software firm, invited her to lunch and insisted on splitting the bill. "We're colleagues now. Equal shares." Lavanya laughed, then realised it was true.
Mid-July. A new intern, Nikhil, froze during his first code review. Lavanya found him later by the water cooler and told him about her own disastrous first review, the one Sarika had talked her through.
Late August. Nikhil messaged Lavanya: "Merged my first feature!" She forwarded it to Sarika with a note: "Passing on what you gave me. Thank you." Sarika's reply was a single line: "That's the whole point 🎉"

qa.q: Where did Lavanya find Nikhil after his first code review?
qa.a: She found him by the water cooler.

qa.q: Why did Lavanya forward Nikhil's message to Sarika?
qa.a: She felt grateful and wanted Sarika to know that her help was now being passed on to someone newer.

qa.q: How did Lavanya pay forward what she received, and why did it work?
qa.a: She shared her own disastrous first review with Nikhil, just as Sarika once talked her through it, which eased his fear and helped him keep going.

qa.q: What does Sarika's reply show about how she sees the circle?
qa.a: Sarika sees mentoring as successful when help moves on to others, and seems proud rather than left behind.

grounding: Over a summer a mentee becomes her mentor's equal and starts guiding a new intern, thanking her mentor by passing the help on.

subtype: Stage 6: Peer and paying it forward [Response]
passage: Arohi, you say you feel strange now that the new trainee calls you 'ma'am'. Let your Dadi, Hansa, tell you something. When I was twenty-five, a nurse at the district hospital, Sister Kamala taught me everything, from finding a tiny vein to calming a frightened father at midnight. Two years later she started asking my opinion on the ward rota. One evening she said, 'Call me Kamala, not Sister.' We drank tea as friends after that, forty years of tea. That same winter a new girl, Mariam, cried in the linen room after losing her first patient. I sat with her the way Kamala once sat with me. When I thanked Kamala, she said, 'Don't thank me. Sit with the next one.' So, beti, sit with your trainee.

qa.q: Where did Mariam cry after losing her first patient?
qa.a: Mariam cried in the linen room.

qa.q: Why did Hansa sit with Mariam in the linen room?
qa.a: She remembered how Kamala had once sat with her and wanted Mariam to feel that same comfort; it was her way of carrying her gratitude forward.

qa.q: What is Dadi advising Arohi to do, and why?
qa.a: To sit with and guide her new trainee, because that is how the help Hansa received from Kamala keeps moving to the next person.

qa.q: How might Kamala have felt seeing Hansa guide Mariam?
qa.a: She would probably feel proud and content, since she saw thanks as best expressed by helping the next one.

grounding: A grandmother recalls her mentor becoming a friend of equals while she began guiding a newer nurse, passing the help on.

subtype: Stage 6: Peer and paying it forward [Response]
passage:
The metro was shut because of the flooding, so Zeenat and Pooja ended up sharing an auto home, knees squashed, rain spraying in from the side.
"You don't call me 'ma'am' any more," Pooja said, laughing.
"You told me to stop two years ago!"
Zeenat's phone buzzed. The new intern, Rhea, stuck at the office: "Sorry to disturb, how do I file the late report?"
Zeenat typed back step by step, the way Pooja once did for her at midnight. Then she added, "Ask me anything. Someone did that for me."
Pooja read it over her shoulder and went quiet. "That's the best thank-you I've had," she said.

qa.q: Why was the metro shut?
qa.a: Because of the flooding.

qa.q: What was Pooja feeling when she read Zeenat's message to Rhea?
qa.a: She felt moved and grateful, seeing her own help being passed on as the best kind of thanks.

qa.q: What small habit could Zeenat keep so the help keeps passing on?
qa.a: Keep answering newer people's questions patiently, as she did for Rhea, even when it's inconvenient.

qa.q: What is it like for Rhea to get Zeenat's reply late at night?
qa.a: Rhea is probably relieved and less alone, stuck at the office but helped step by step.

grounding: Shows a former mentor and mentee as equals, while the mentee guides a newer intern and the mentor feels thanked by it.

subtype: Stage 6: Peer and paying it forward [Response]
passage:
Irfan and Hemant met every second Saturday now, at the same Irani café near the old office, and they split the bill without arguing. Five years earlier, Hemant had been the nervous trainee and Irfan the manager who covered for his mistakes. Now they argued about cricket and swapped book recommendations.
This Saturday Hemant was late. He came in with a young man carrying a laptop bag. "Irfan, this is Sid. First job, second week. I told him you'd scare him less than I do."
Irfan laughed and pulled out a chair. As Sid talked, Irfan watched Hemant answer the questions himself, patiently, the way Irfan once had. He didn't interrupt once.

qa.q: How often do Irfan and Hemant meet now?
qa.a: Every second Saturday.

qa.q: What might Irfan be feeling as he watches Hemant answer Sid's questions?
qa.a: He likely feels proud and quietly moved, seeing Hemant pass on the patience he once showed him.

qa.q: Why was Irfan not interrupting a good choice at this stage?
qa.a: It let Hemant guide Sid as an equal and mentor in his own right, instead of slipping back into being the boss.

qa.q: What is it like for Sid, in his second week, to sit with them?
qa.a: Sid is probably nervous but reassured to be welcomed and taken seriously by two experienced people.

grounding: Shows a mentoring bond turned into a friendship of equals, with the former mentee now guiding someone newer.

subtype: Stage 6: Peer and paying it forward [Response]
passage:
"Harish, you're the one who taught me to write a proper handover note."
"And you're the one who taught me to stop sending emails at midnight, Anand. We're even."
They were at Harish's balcony, two cups of chai, the city humming below.
"I've got a new joinee," Anand said. "Keeps apologising for everything."
"Sounds like someone I knew."
"Exactly. So I've been doing what you did. Weekly coffee. No judging questions."
Harish put his cup down. "You know, when you did that, it felt better than any thank-you card."
"That's the idea. I couldn't pay you back. So I'm paying it on."

qa.q: Where were Harish and Anand sitting?
qa.a: On Harish's balcony.

qa.q: Why did Anand start weekly coffees with the new joinee?
qa.a: He felt grateful to Harish and wanted to pass on the same help, recognising his old nervous self in the joinee.

qa.q: What makes this stage of the relationship healthy?
qa.a: They teach each other as equals, and Anand turns his gratitude into guiding someone newer.

qa.q: How does Harish feel about Anand mentoring someone else?
qa.a: Harish feels touched and proud, saying it meant more than any thank-you card.

grounding: Shows a mentor and former mentee as equal friends, with the mentee expressing gratitude by guiding a new joinee.

subtype: Stage 6: Peer and paying it forward [Response]
passage: Harsha and I had dinner last Friday, and for the first time I noticed that I paid my own share without either of us thinking about it. Four years ago she was my senior at the lab, the one who taught me to label every sample twice and not to cry when an experiment failed. Now we argue about novels, and she asks my opinion on her research proposals. Somewhere along the way we became friends. Then on Monday a new junior, Ankur, stood at my bench looking lost, holding a pipette as if it might bite. I heard myself say, "Label everything twice. And come to me when it fails, not if." That evening I messaged Harsha: "Just said your line to someone new. Thank you, for all of it." She wrote back, "That's the whole point, Reena."

qa.q: What did Harsha teach about samples?
qa.a: To label every sample twice.

qa.q: How did Reena feel sending the message to Harsha?
qa.a: Reena felt grateful and warm, moved to realise that Harsha's help was now being passed on.

qa.q: How does Reena's action show the circle continuing?
qa.a: Reena guides Ankur with Harsha's own advice and thanks Harsha, showing gratitude by passing on the help received.

qa.q: What might Ankur be experiencing at Reena's bench?
qa.a: Ankur seems lost and nervous, and is probably relieved to hear a senior invite him to come for help when things fail.

grounding: Shows a mentoring bond becoming a friendship of equals, and the former mentee starting to guide someone newer out of gratitude.
